thread.title: Chicago heat leaves Lake Shore Drive bridge stuck open - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Chicago heat leaves Lake Shore Drive bridge stuck open - NewsBreak

author: Emilee Speck
title: Chicago heat leaves Lake Shore Drive bridge stuck open - NewsBreak
text:
By Emilee Speck ,
7 hours ago A Chicago fireboat sprayed water on the DuSable Lake Shore Drive Bridge after a heat-related malfunction snarled traffic Wednesday.
Extreme heat caused one of Chicago ’s busiest bridges to malfunction Wednesday, leaving the structure partially raised and bringing traffic along DuSable Lake Shore Drive to a standstill.
The bridge over the Chicago River was raised around 10 a.m. CDT as part of a scheduled lift to provide river access for the Spirit of Chicago cruise ship. However, the bridge failed to close completely afterward.
“During a scheduled bridge lift this morning, the DLSD bridge experienced a heat-related issue preventing it from fully closing,” the Chicago Department of Transportation said in a statement. “Crews are making the necessary adjustments to safely close the bridge and reopen the roadway as quickly as possible.”
A Chicago Fire Department boat was seen spraying water onto the bridge around 11:40 a.m., apparently in an effort to cool the structure. High temperatures can cause metal bridge components to expand, potentially preventing movable sections from aligning properly.
DuSable Lake Shore Drive and Lower Wacker Drive were closed near the bridge as crews worked on the malfunction. Northbound traffic was diverted at Jackson Drive, while southbound drivers were directed off at Grand Avenue, according to WLS .
The bridge was raised again for another scheduled lift at 12:15 p.m. Crews subsequently tested the structure, but it was not immediately clear when the roadway would reopen.
The malfunction unfolded as dangerous heat and humidity gripped Chicago and surrounding communities.
"The bridge malfunction occurred shortly after its scheduled 10 a.m. lift, at a time when the heat was already rapidly building across Chicago," AccuWeather Meteorologist Chad Erikson said. "When the bridge failed to close after it's 10 a.m. lift, temperatures were already around 86 degrees. The high temperature in Chicago is expected to be 96 degrees this afternoon. The incident came during on ongoing stretch of late-season heat across the Chicago area."
Chicago was under a heat advisory that covered much of northern Illinois from noon until 9 p.m. CDT Wednesday. AccuWeather RealFeel® Temperatures were expected to reach 100 to 105 degrees.
The advisory covered central and northern Cook County, including Chicago, as well as Boone, DeKalb, DuPage, Kane, Lake, Lee, McHenry, Ogle and Winnebago counties.
Forecasters warned that the combination of high temperatures and oppressive humidity could cause heat-related illnesses, particularly for people spending extended periods outdoors.
